1	# Direct the film before describing its look
2	
3	Owner instruction, October 7th, 2026. Active for newly planned editions from October 8th,
4	or an explicit `film_direction` opt-in. The original source, rights, minimum action,
5	native PNG/CRF16, audio, caption, independent panel and autonomous shipment gates remain.
6	
7	## What the previous upgrade failed to change
8	
9	October 7th's shipped film passed its mechanical gates and scored 7.596. The owner rejected
10	its engagement and pace. It repeated an equipment tableau through six scenes, with a 9.5-second
11	closing scene. Palette, camera poses and declared events did not create a visual argument.
12	The bounded release contract could also defer pacing, motion, surface finish and ending artistry.
13	Neither a score nor a completed worksheet overrules that observed failure.
14	
15	This upgrade therefore changes the executable route and review eligibility. It does not promise
16	an aesthetic result from a new renderer name. Current production uses `directed-film-v2` and a
17	registered, story-specific episode. Missing plans, unknown views and legacy routes fail. Older
18	episodes remain reproducible as historical evidence. A current film cannot defer the four
19	categories above, even at a creative ceiling. Capacity recovery funds mandatory repair on the
20	current route; it never restores the retired route or edits a rejected finding.
21	
22	## Lessons verified in AlaskaAIWeekly
23	
24	Study pinned source and complete published films, rather than an isolated hero still. The current
25	reference revision is `e53f3f92e6cbe123e8802239d8172622d4f3a630`.
26	
27	- [Directors room](https://github.com/Talonsturgill/alaska-ai-weekly/blob/e53f3f92e6cbe123e8802239d8172622d4f3a630/prompts/dispatch_routine.md)
28	  commits an earned angle, cold open, escalation, performed turn and visual button. Translate its
29	  contrasting dramatic, comic, explanatory and curious lenses into the existing two complete
30	  Texas treatments. Do not add daily roles, extra pitches or another paid panel.
31	- [October 7th episode](https://github.com/Talonsturgill/alaska-ai-weekly/blob/e53f3f92e6cbe123e8802239d8172622d4f3a630/video-engine/src/Ep1007.tsx)
32	  uses a recurring physical object, distinct shot sizes, local reactions, carefully finished
33	  silhouettes and named visual reveals. A figure's state changes across scenes; the frame does
34	  not merely rescan the same equipment.
35	- [October 6th episode](https://github.com/Talonsturgill/alaska-ai-weekly/blob/e53f3f92e6cbe123e8802239d8172622d4f3a630/video-engine/src/Ep1006.tsx)
36	  gives its desk and phone a visual performance, with local anticipation, contact and result.
37	  Port that causal grammar and reusable finished assets. Do not copy its regional mascot,
38	  factual claims, source archive, ledger or old footage into Texas.
39	- The current Alaska master also corrects its old instruction to punctuate every beat with a
40	  camera kick. Preserve motivated cuts and object reactions. Frequent new information does not
41	  mean perpetual shake, strobing, overshoot or arbitrary camera motion.
42	
43	## Two complete treatments, one executable direction
44	
45	Before voice, design exactly two feasible, complete alternatives. Each needs a first-frame
46	question, a recognizable throughline subject, an escalation, a fair source-backed turn, a
47	closing picture that answers the opening, and a sound arc. Different shot ordering, staging
48	and visual emphasis must give a viewer a different experience. Two camera poses on the same
49	tableau are one treatment.
50	
51	Write `film_direction` with the active policy version, registered episode, actual renderer
52	hashes, angle, opening promise, performed turn, closing answer, shot timeline and rewards.
53	The shot timeline covers every story frame, conserves subject identity and source-bound scene
54	timing, and names an implemented view and overlapping physical event. Use at least three useful
55	framings. A new action, reaction, comparison, consequence or evidence reveal earns each cut.
56	An empty push, rotating fan or appearing label alone does not count as new understanding.
57	
58	Before code review, freeze each shot's `scene_fraction_start` and `scene_fraction_end` within its source
59	scene, and each reward's `event_fraction` within its physical event. These authored anchors
60	belong to the approved concept. `board_retime.py` derives the measured seconds from them after
61	voice alignment, without compounding earlier timing. If the measured read breaks the limits
62	or event overlap, repair the edit; never stretch the narration or silently move a reward.
63	
64	The current product limits are in `config/modern_film.json`: first visible change within 1.5
65	seconds, no shot longer than 5 seconds, and no unearned information interval longer than 4
66	seconds. These are explicit production constraints chosen after the owner rejection, not a
67	scientific claim about all audiences. Do not bypass them by relabeling a repeated view or
68	inventing event declarations. Independent review watches the execution at normal speed.
69	
70	Generate this edition's fresh hero and supporting artwork under STORY_ART.md before animation.
71	Finish the hero silhouette, contact shadows, layered surfaces, motivated light and focal hierarchy
72	at native size and 390-pixel phone width before voice. Use authentic licensed footage when it
73	provides useful action. Otherwise author a source-bound illustration. Do not infer a particular
74	failure mechanism, measured value, actual operator, hardware design or completed outcome.
75	
76	## Perform and judge the complete edit
77	
78	Narration is an energetic, continuous explanation with purposeful contrasts. Begin the action
79	immediately, keep connective phrases moving, and reserve emphasis and breathing room for the
80	turn and answer. Do not put a reverent pause after every clause. Shorten slow writing before
81	synthesis, rather than accelerating the audio. Compare actual take timing with the approved
82	shot rewards and listen through the existing audiovisual path. Fast unreadable words fail too.
83	
84	The existing phone critic and three separate final scorers receive this guide's actual text and
85	hash. At visual/final scope each returns exact-film `modern_observations` for first frame, visual
86	progression, shot variety, performed turn, pace, closing answer and finished art. Each contains
87	an observed interval, concrete finding and pass flag. The ordinary rubric and actual failures
88	remain unchanged. A high average cannot replace a failed engagement or finish observation.
89	
90	Optional engineering stops at its reserved boundary. If a mandatory current-route observation
91	fails, preserve that cut and repair through the configured autonomous completion policy, using
92	the retained independent source-backed pivot when needed. Neither artistic ceilings nor host
93	capacity authorize a legacy episode, slideshow rescue or unaudited provider substitution.
94	
95	
96	## The region stands behind every current film
97	
98	Owner instruction, October 9th, 2026, on the plan's fifth step. Place was the show's weakest axis
99	(6.36 on the mean of the last ten report cards) and every current film stood in a flat gradient,
100	so a Harris County story and a Reeves County story looked like the same nowhere.
101	
102	From the date in `video-engine/src/modern/placePlates.json` (`policy.effective_date`), DirectedFilm
103	draws each scene's region behind its episode through `modern/PlaceStage.tsx`. Each of the ten
104	regions has a plate, rendered once in the Docket's carousel engine from a scene page under
105	`assets/place/scenes/` by `scripts/place_bake.py`, as a sky, one ground and cards for the things
106	standing on it. The bake measured that the layers reassemble into the picture and that every
107	camera profile keeps the ground covering the frame and every base on its ground. The manifest
108	records those measurements, the Docket commit, every layer's sha256 and the hash of each module a
109	scene imports from `assets/place/`. Water is drawn by `assets/place/water.js` as a mirror of the
110	world in its own plane, because a lake seen from eye height under a hazy sky otherwise reads as a
111	pale slab, and no scatter grows on it.
112	
113	- **The plate is the county's when it has one, and the region's when it doesn't.** A region's own
114	  plate carries nothing that belongs to one place, no skyline and no refinery, because a Texan is
115	  not told they live somewhere they don't. Harris County stands in Houston across Buffalo Bayou,
116	  Dallas County over the Trinity floodplain, Travis County across Lady Bird Lake and Bexar County
117	  over the river south of downtown. A story at a plant on the upper coast names
118	  `place_plate: "gulf-shipchannel"` on its scenes for the refineries, which a board may do only for
119	  a county that plate lists. The fly gene film's labs are in the Medical Center, and a blind grade
120	  of its frames on October 9th marked the refinery view as the wrong place within the right county.
121	- **Outdoors** the plate fills the frame and the camera moves through it on the scene's
122	  `camera_strategy`, within a share of the plate's measured limits. The ground moves by the exact
123	  perspective transform, so it never tears. Wrap a subject that stands on the ground in
124	  `<PlaceSubject baseY={...}>` with the frame row its base touches, and it rides with its ground.
125	  Keep type and overlays outside it.
126	- **Indoors, wide and medium**, the region is outside a window in the back wall. It starts below
127	  the title band, it is held still and it is bright and soft, the way a camera exposed for the room
128	  sees a window, behind a light frame. The episode draws its own floor and props in front of it.
129	- **Indoors, close and detail**, there is no window, only its light: the region is a soft wash
130	  behind the subject, because a lens that close is focused on the subject and a window pane behind
131	  a fly makes the fly as tall as the pane. Any view the episode lists in `wash_views` takes the same
132	  wash at every framing. List a labelled comparison there, things set out on their own ground lines
133	  with a label over each, since a window's rails and skyline cross exactly that type and those lines.
134	- **Overhead**, and any view the episode lists in `wall_views` (a diagram or a document, which is
135	  not in a room), keep plain wall. No more than 40 percent of a film's shots may be wall views.
136	
137	**An episode never paints a full-frame background.** That one rect hides the whole region, and
138	the film looks exactly as it did when place was the weakest axis. Paint the floor, the props and
139	anything the story needs in the room. `scripts/place_check.py --render` renders every shot with the
140	plate as solid magenta and fails a shot that shows less than its minimum share of region, by
141	name. Unboxed type over the window stays dark or gets its own panel, as type over any picture does.
142	
143	The stage also draws a county locator from two seconds in. A small card draws the state's outline,
144	fills the first scene's county and rings it, on the vetted map-explainer timing (border 2.5
145	seconds, fill 1.0, label 0.7). It carries no words, because no claim stands behind a board's
146	county and the narration names the place. Its map is computed by `scripts/county_map.py`.
147	
148	A run never bakes a plate. A plate is added or changed by editing its scene page and running
149	`place_bake.py --docket <a TexasAIDocket checkout>`, and the layers and manifest are committed
150	together. CI fails a scene or a place module edited without a re-bake. Each plate names the engine
151	record it was drawn with, the Docket commit and the bytes of every engine file, so a plate rebaked
152	alone with a newer Docket leaves every other plate's record as it was. The bake measures the layers
153	as the stage loads them, encoded as lossless WebP and read back, and holds each limit to its
154	measurements: the last step that passed, the next step's failure and every profile end the stage
155	moves to. CI measures cover and magnification again from the committed layers at every profile end
156	and requires the bake's numbers exactly. Open each baked plate's `out/place-bake/<plate>/full.png`
157	at film size before committing it: the bake measures whether the layers move as one world, never
158	whether the water reads as water.
159	
160	## Narration and picture use one clock
161	
162	For new production from October 8th, every spoken clause has a narration-picture-v1 binding in board.narration_picture. Write exact clause text, concrete subject_ids, executable action_id, source claim_ids, scene_id, cue_ids and event_ids before voice production. Cover all words and qualifiers once in their original order. The registered episode declares which views actually implement those subjects and actions. A topic match, caption or label cannot replace a pictured causal step.
163	
164	Before voice exists, use timing_mode authored with an explicit provisional cue plan for the silent two-treatment comparison. These estimated windows approve only planning. After alignment, board_retime.py replaces them with measured_caption_boundaries from the actual captions and acoustic word stream. Timed capture, preship and delivery require those measured inputs and reject an authored clock.
165	
166	After acoustic alignment, compile every clause window from complete measured caption boundaries and the matched positional word stream. Use modern_film.compile_narration with the actual captions and words. Derive cut handoffs from silence between clauses. Only framing subdivisions inside the same subject/action may use fractions. Renderer performances consume requireNarration on the film-global clock, and retain completed consequences across cuts. Never stretch speech, scale cue times, or proportionally place a different narrated action inside a scene.
167	
168	Run scripts/modern_film.py with --board, --captions, --words, --script and --claims before timed capture and preship. The gate rejects missing or duplicated clauses, omitted qualifiers, stale timing, wrong condition identity, incompatible renderer views and gaps in matching picture coverage. These checks establish bindings, not audience understanding. Code, phone and final reviewers inspect the actual subject and performed action for every clause. Return narration_picture_observations bound to the exact film, with ordered clauses containing id, pass, exact start_s/end_s and observed. Preserve a wrong or absent picture as a source/comprehension blocker even if provider metadata says pass.
169	
170	A current clause must remain understandable with its captions covered. Introduce the spoken subject before its clause begins, perform the narrated change while it is heard, and retain the relevant result through the clause end. Distinguish selection, analysis, test condition, observed result and clinical limit. Generic clinical forms, a repeated test picture under an AI-selection line, or the normal condition under a patient-variant line fail this contract.
171

1	# Direct a world before building a scene
2	
3	Teaching sources: [Pixar's cinematography account](https://renderman.pixar.com/stories/incredible-cinematography)
4	for coordinated staging, light and camera; [OpenAI evaluation practices](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/evaluation-best-practices)
5	for reference calibration, pairwise comparison and order bias. Current filmed evidence decides
6	which choices work here.
7	
8	Read this with the viewer method, selected approach dossier, fixed quality contract and
9	current rubric. It adds executable craft inputs and calibration, not a score, quota,
10	new judge or extra paid attempt. Existing source, rights, action, native, audio, captions,
11	cumulative resources, finite artistic recovery and shipment requirements continue.
12	
13	## Director
14	
15	Before coding, choose the visual approach from actual source access. Think through four
16	lenses in the existing director assignment: the comedian finds an observable mismatch;
17	the dramatist finds pressure and a changed state; the explainer finds the causal relation;
18	the enthusiast finds a specific surprising detail. Do not invent a joke, conflict or
19	outcome. Choose exactly two complete treatments within the current comparison allowance.
20	
21	Write `art_direction` in each board using `config/art_direction.json`. Explain seven palette
22	roles, contrasting shapes, the recognizable hero silhouette and its finish, motivated
23	light, focal hierarchy, action timing, and one signature shot tied to an actual event.
24	Name the current asset and actual subject ids. Use the source image itself when it is the
25	hero. Give a dimensional scene a `shots[scene_id]` camera position, target, lens and reason;
26	an event-bound `to` pose is optional. For the illustrated carton route, use `flat_shots`
27	with native-coordinate offsets, scale and a reason. Numeric shot choices must be executed
28	by the routed scene, not left as board prose. A custom renderer must consume the same
29	profile or explain its retained source lighting and implement its relevant choices.
30	
31	The focal object stays sharp. Depth blur must arise from actual separation and preserve
32	contact detail. Never add blur, floating shapes, lens flares, camera kicks or orbiting as
33	automatic cinematic decoration. Hold the camera while an object performs. Move it to reveal
34	a relation or follow a finite action. Give a completed result a comprehension hold.
35	
36	## Scene builder and render owner
37	
38	Use `prompts/roles/scene-builder.md` in the existing code assignment. Build the finished
39	hero first, then light and stage it before extending the scene. Recognizable geometry,
40	edges, seams, hardware, texture and grounded shadows beat a field of placeholder primitives.
41	Authored 2.5D, useful footage and a readable source image can outperform complicated 3D.
42	Do not restrict the daily story to the demonstration subject or copy reference b-roll.
43	
44	The shared `ArtDirectionProvider` carries current choices in both entry points. Three.js
45	`CinematicStage`/`Studio` execute the light recipe and exposure. `directedShot` executes
46	authored event-bound cameras. The illustrated carton component executes its flat framing,
47	finished surfaces, occlusion and contact assemblies. Source footage retains original speed
48	and practical lighting. Existing boards without this profile retain their original defaults.
49	
50	Every new event specifies a motion curve within its existing measured window: `travel`
51	accelerates and brakes; `contact` approaches and settles; `linear` serves constant-speed
52	movement; `smoothstep` is available for a justified gentle transition. `anticipation` and
53	`settle` reserve fractions inside that window, never new runtime or voice stretching.
54	`landing` has a small overshoot and needs a free-prop reason; never use it for a constrained
55	contact, a foot planted on ground, or a source-implied machine limit. Check music and foley
56	against the executed contact, not the old curve. No incidental sway substitutes for action.
57	
58	Judge motion at the delivered 30 fps. A regular frame clock does not excuse abrupt starts,
59	fast screen-space travel or repeated stop-and-go strokes. Directed `travel` and `contact`
60	curves start and finish with zero velocity and acceleration. Give a heavy load enough of
61	the existing scene window to accelerate and brake. Holds consume that window; do not squeeze
62	the entire stroke into the remaining few frames. Inspect velocity at event joins as well
63	as the start and end. Keep a clear contact view and a stable camera when tracking amplifies
64	the load's movement. Do not conceal stepping with blur, frame interpolation or faster audio.
65	An event-bound moving camera uses `travel` or `contact`; the input check refuses constant-speed
66	starts and landing overshoot on a camera. Hold it when the object needs a different curve.
67

1	# Make the editorial choice before the picture
2	
3	Apply this method to newly planned editions from October 3rd, 2026. It guides decisions under the current contracts and does not certify quality. It adds no board schema, scorer, research pass or paid attempt.
4	
5	## Decide and record
6	
7	Read the selector and chosen approach dossier in full. For a news report also read the reporting dossier. Use the existing creative_direction and story_contract fields; keep the decision rationale compact and inspectable.
8	
9	1. **Focus.** In viewer_question and visible_answer, state what changes, for whom, through which sourced action. Name the expected viewer takeaway and the strongest honest limit. Distinguish the narrative answer from an unknown eventual outcome.
10	2. **Choose.** Begin medium_choice with the named format and approach: News report, Educational explainer or Cinematic scene; then Observed documentary, Explanatory animation, Evidence-led imagery or Cinematic scene. Explain why the available assets can carry the explanation and why a plausible alternative is weaker. Naming an approach is a routing aid, not an approval field.
11	3. **Order.** Put each beat's reporting job in the existing scene advances and edit notes. For a report choose human-led, mechanism-led or evidence-led ordering. Explain why this evidence appears here and what question it creates or answers. Educational explanation builds a recognizable example through successive states. A cinematic scene follows a task, obstacle, consequential turn and completed action. Do not apply one rundown to all three.
12	4. **Anticipate confusion.** Name the most likely false inference and the picture or immediate source limit that prevents it. In emotional_turn, connect the viewer's changing understanding to an evidenced stake. Do not invent a person's feelings or claim to know the audience's reaction.
13	5. **Connect.** In enter_on, leave_on, cut_after_event_id and next_connection, name the visible event, new information and carried subject. Complete the event before the cut. A footage-to-diagram handoff keeps the same identified example or discloses a new one. Finish the sentence-to-shot worksheet inside these existing notes.
14	6. **Direct and test.** Tie line intent, emphasis, motivated sound and captions to the actual reveal. Before spending, ask what remains understandable with narration muted and editorial labels covered, then test the combined account. Essential dates and attribution can use text; the principal action must read in the picture. Budget the entire remaining review/render path, including independent-provider recovery where required.
15	
16	These are short decision reasons a colleague can inspect, not a request for a private stream of thought. Use concrete evidence and an alternative that could realistically be built. Do not fill every field with the same sentence, duplicate the research or commission a third treatment.
17	
18	## Each worker has a distinct decision
19	
20	- **Researcher:** Identify the most informative picture and the strongest limitation. Recommend an angle that the assets can actually show; flag the sentence for which no truthful picture exists.
21	- **Director:** Choose the story focus, format, medium and order. Resolve the weak handoff before narration, using the same two-treatment batch and consolidated ledger.
22	- **VO director:** Translate the approved beat jobs into a continuous performance. Explain a lift, drop or pause through the reveal it supports; preserve the words and alignment.
23	- **Code critic:** Determine whether the proposed implementation can perform the action and carry the explanation. A planned gesture is not a watched result.
24	- **Phone critic and scorers:** First describe what is recognizable and what changes in the actual film. Then compare with the approved account. Locate the weakest identity or information handoff and classify the observed defect under the existing criteria. Keep their separate assigned lenses and actual verdicts.
25	
26	For remote independent recovery, the supplied packet contains the actual method, selector, reporting dossier and named approach text. If a director has not named an approach, all four approach guides are supplied rather than pretending an unread local path was available. The new teaching bundle is added only for editions from October 3rd. A text packet never establishes audiovisual access.
27	
28	## Why the handoff needs thought
29	
30	An original film-comprehension study associated event boundaries with meaningful changes in characters, objects, place, goals and causes. Our application is to preserve those relationships across a cut and make a change understandable. This is an editorial inference, not a scientifically established short-video pacing interval or retention guarantee. [Zacks and colleagues, The Brain's Cutting-Room Floor](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/human-neuroscience/articles/10.3389/fnhum.2010.00168/full).
31	
32	The director can consult the [observed news examples](broadcast-cadence-study.md) when a reporting choice needs a model. Workers use the supplied method, relevant guide and current artifacts without repeatedly reloading the research corpus. Retain real rejections; a well-written plan can't clear absent action, false implication or failed comprehension.

1	# Visual storytelling for Dispatch
2	
3	Research and direction revision: October 2nd, 2026.
4	
5	The picture, narration and captions must describe the same unfolding story. The picture supplies a recognizable subject, relationship, action or consequence. Narration explains its significance and limits. Captions give access to the spoken account. A moving object is useful only when the viewer understands what it represents and what its change means.
6	
7	These dossiers combine researched craft with proposed Dispatch practice. Source observations are identified and linked. The shot methods, selection procedure and worked example are our production recommendations, not claims that research guarantees audience engagement.
8	
9	## Choose the story's visual approach
10	
11	Read this index and the chosen dossier in full before boarding. Select by the available evidence and the explanation the viewer needs. Keep one primary approach; supporting footage or documents should connect to that approach through a clear subject or question.
12	
13	| Approach | Choose when | What it must show | Reject when |
14	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
15	| [Observed documentary](observed-documentary.md) | Authenticated footage shows the actual people, place, equipment or workflow | A real action and its observed result | Similar-looking stock replaces the story's actual identity |
16	| [Explanatory animation](explanatory-animation.md) | The central process or comparison is hard to see directly | Recognizable input, meaningful transformation and readable output | Abstract objects require a private legend to decode |
17	| [Evidence-led imagery](evidence-led-imagery.md) | Relevant photographs or documents carry the reporting | What the evidence establishes and how it changes the answer | A sequence of screenshots substitutes for the entire mechanism |
18	| [Cinematic scene](cinematic-scene.md) | A source-backed physical task, obstacle and consequence can sustain a scene | Spatially coherent action, a turn and a consequential ending | Lighting, orbiting props or music replace story development |
19	
20	Use this selection order:
21	
22	1. State the viewer's question, sourced action, affected person or group and honest ending.
23	2. Inventory inspected, usable assets and demonstrated components. Record what each can and can't show.
24	3. Choose the approach that makes the central relationship easiest to understand. Explain the rejected alternative in one sentence.
25	4. Complete the [sentence-to-shot worksheet](sentence-to-shot.md). Resolve missing pictures before locking narration.
26	5. Compare exactly two genuinely different complete treatments in the existing shared preview batch. Read the selected dossier for each treatment. Preserve the current contracts, frozen budget and existing independent roles.
27	6. Have the existing critic inspect the actual rendered sequence before reading the director's explanation. A filled worksheet does not prove comprehension.
28	
29	Do not impose a weekday rotation. Track the selected approach in the existing creative-direction rationale so the director can see recent repetition. When two approaches fit equally well, variety can break the tie. Never choose variety at the expense of truth or comprehension.
30	
31	## Choose a format and think through its sequence
32	
33	For newly planned editions from October 3rd, read the [viewer planning method](viewer-plan.md) in full. Distinguish the format from the medium: a news report can use observed footage, illustration or documents; an educational explainer can return from a diagram to physical evidence; a cinematic scene still needs a truthful task and consequence.
34	
35	For a news report read [the reporting dossier](news-reporting.md) and choose its human-led, mechanism-led or evidence-led structure from the actual story. Record why the order works, the likely false inference and the carried subject across each cut in the existing creative-direction and transition fields. The [national-news study](broadcast-cadence-study.md) identifies the observed examples and access limits. It does not prescribe a single bracketed rundown.
36	
37	The director and workers use these short decision reasons to choose and challenge the treatment. A copied structure, named style or completed worksheet supplies no quality verdict. The packet tools bind the current method and relevant approach text; remote recovery supplies the actual text because a provider can't open local links.
38	
39	## Give the three channels distinct jobs
40	
41	**See:** Show the thing being discussed at the moment it is discussed. Preserve its identity across the cut. Make any comparison legible before asking the viewer to infer a result.
42	
43	**Hear:** Name the relationship, cause or uncertainty that the picture can't establish alone. Time emphasis and event sound to the actual reveal. A music swell can't supply an unreported outcome.
44	
45	**Read:** Retain complete measured captions. Use brief object labels only where they identify a picture or distinction. Avoid simultaneous paragraph copy competing with both the action and captions. Lay out the decisive result above the real caption band and hold it long enough to understand.
46	
47	Mayer's research summary supports removing distracting content, placing related words near pictures and presenting corresponding animation and narration together. It also reports redundancy effects in multimedia learning. These are learning findings, not a forecast of short-video retention; they do not justify removing accessible captions. Our application is to reduce competing editorial text while maintaining captions. [Cambridge multimedia-learning chapter](https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/abs/cambridge-handbook-of-multimedia-learning/principles-for-reducing-extraneous-processing-in-multimedia-learning-coherence-signaling-redundancy-spatial-contiguity-and-temporal-contiguity-principles/C98AB3A6CE760DD63C048936EA0B3B44), [W3C caption guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/captions-prerecorded).
48	
49	## Review what the viewer receives
50	
51	Use the existing review assignments and fixed rubric. Add these observations to their existing consolidated notes, not a new scorecard or paid role.
52	
53	- **Recognition:** Before reading the board, what does the principal object look like? Can the critic name it without guessing?
54	- **Alignment:** At each narrated clause, does the picture show the named subject and relationship? Record exact film times for contradictions or absent concepts.
55	- **Development:** What changed, and how does that change lead to the next shot? Distinguish subject transformation from decorative motion.
56	- **Continuity:** Is the same person, site, sample or document being followed? Is a different example disclosed?
57	- **Combined comprehension:** After one viewing with audio and captions, what happened, who can act and what remains unproven?
58	- **Picture contribution:** With narration muted and captions covered, which parts of the central process can the viewer actually see? Dates and attribution may rely on text; the principal action can't.
59	- **Ending:** Does the final picture answer the opening question without inventing implementation, savings, approval or repair?
60	
61	An unrecognizable object, absent principal action or contradictory picture is a comprehension/source defect under the current contract. Do not classify it as merely style because pixels move. Surface polish and optional camera preferences remain artistic issues. Retain all real rejected verdicts and use the existing repair and bounded-release policies.
62	
63	## Apply this without expanding production
64	
65	Use the current budget precheck for the complete review and render path before spending. Keep the bounded visual search, source and rights evidence, prior-edition identity gate, two-treatment comparison, native hero, phone inspection, audiovisual lenses and independent scorers. The dossiers introduce no render quota, new reviewer or budget extension.
66	
67	Read [the October 2nd diagnosis and proposed sequence](october-2-pavement-case.md) for the difference between a source-related object and a picture that communicates the spoken claim.
68	
69	## Research status
70	
71	Sources were accessed October 2nd, 2026. The four approach dossiers use published guidance, research summaries and practitioner accounts; their linked film examples are references rather than claimed viewing. The separate national-news study adds explicitly scoped transcripts and rendered samples. Today's diagnosis uses the listed native frame samples and retained board; it is not a replacement independent whole-film review. Research access does not grant reuse rights to any publisher's images, footage or soundtrack.

1	# Direct a coherent news report
2	
3	The [cadence study](broadcast-cadence-study.md) records the evidence behind this dossier. The structures below are Dispatch production choices, not a universal network script. Apply them to newly planned editions from October 3rd, 2026; preserve shipped editions and their real reviews.
4	
5	A report has an editorial spine: a specific situation, a question, evidence that changes the answer, an explanation, an honest consequence and a close. Decide which of those jobs the next shot performs. A source-related image that supplies no new understanding is a weak insert, even if its colors and motion look expensive.
6	
7	## Choose the order from the story
8	
9	| Reporting structure | Choose it when | Sequence of reporting jobs | Ending test |
10	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
11	| Human-led report | The evidence identifies a real person's task, obstacle or changed options | Show the task or consequence → establish the dated change → broaden with evidence → explain the cause and limits → return to the same person or task | Has the viewer learned what changes for that person, without an invented reaction or outcome? |
12	| Mechanism-led report | The central news is a process, measurement or decision that viewers can't readily see | Show a recognizable input and question → orient the source and setting → reveal the transformation → show the result → connect it to a human decision and its limits | Can the viewer explain the input, transformation and result, and distinguish an illustration from observed operation? |
13	| Evidence-led report | A filing, policy, measurement or public record changes the reported answer | Establish the dated decision or disputed claim → expose the decisive source detail → explain its effect with a concrete relationship → show affected options or activity → state the unresolved point and next decision | Does the ending answer what the record establishes, who can act next and what it does not establish? |
14	
15	Choose one structure. Compress or reorder it when the evidence and viewer's question justify that choice. Establish the essential source limitation when the affected claim appears; a later caveat can't undo a misleading picture. Keep the current early-picture payoff and event timing requirements. These sequences introduce no extra scenes, prescribed shot seconds or runtime quota.
16	
17	The CBS transcript in the study provides a specific-to-broad-to-specific example. The CNN transcript shows a different package organization, and the MSNBC example is a question-led interview. They are different forms with different access to people and evidence. A short Dispatch should not imitate a lengthy panel simply because it resembles national television.
18	
19	## Assign each ingredient a reporting job
20	
21	**Opening:** Give the viewer something identifiable to understand immediately: a task interrupted, an input changing, a decision confronting evidence, or a completed consequence that creates a question. State the actual question soon enough to guide the picture. A dramatic claim must stay within the fetched evidence. Do not borrow an unrelated victim, emergency or reaction to manufacture stakes.
22	
23	**Orientation:** Establish who, where and what changed using the minimum needed narration and labels. This is the short-video equivalent of the paragraph that explains the focus of an article. The viewer should know why the next piece of evidence belongs in this story.
24	
25	**Reporter or presenter:** Use an actual reusable field passage when it demonstrates, verifies or bridges the explanation. A fabricated journalist, microphone prop or studio cut adds no verification. Dispatch's narrator can orient the viewer without appearing as a reporter. A person on screen must have a source-backed role and perform an understandable action.
26	
27	**Evidence:** Show the exact place, equipment, task, relevant photograph or decisive source words. Identify what the evidence establishes. A quotation is evidence of what its speaker said; it is not proof that their conclusion is true. Show a contrary finding or uncertainty when the story requires it. Use the existing source and rights lanes for every asset.
28	
29	**Explanation:** Introduce coded visuals when they reveal a relationship that the authentic image can't show. Keep the same physical subject or explicitly identify the new example. The diagram should answer the question created by the preceding shot. Return to the source image or human decision after the explanation when that return completes the thought.
30	
31	**Consequence and close:** Show how the action changes a state, choice, risk or next step. Answer the opening question through the completed visible action. Distinguish a demonstrated consequence, an expected effect and an unknown eventual outcome. Do not repeat the introduction merely to make the film seem circular. A return earns its place when the viewer now understands the original subject differently.
32	
33	## Move between authentic pictures and coded explanation
34	
35	Make each handoff explicit in the existing edit notes. Carry a stable identifying detail: the same road patch, sample, site, device, document passage or clearly disclosed example. Preserve orientation, useful scale and the relationship under explanation. An outline or highlight identifies a region; it does not prove that a machine detected, measured or classified it.
36	
37	For example, an authenticated image can establish the input. An explicitly illustrated transformation can explain the source-supported relationship. A return to the actual task can show who uses the result. Cutting from an unrelated office image to anonymous blocks and then to a different city breaks that connection, even if every image is broadly about AI.
38	
39	Original illustration is a valid principal medium. Useful footage is also valid. An irrelevant insert should be omitted within the existing bounded search. Do not commission an unproven rig or prolong the stock hunt to imitate a particular outlet. Use the current source-backed action admission when a genuinely necessary mechanism needs implementation.
40	
41	## Direct the cadence across picture, voice and reading
42	
43	Give each beat one new idea the viewer needs for the next beat. Complete its decisive event before cutting. Preserve enough time to recognize the subject, follow the change and read the result. Trim repeated setup before requesting faster narration. Pace varies with information and action; a cut on a fixed timer is not an editorial reason.
44	
45	Voice should orient, reveal, explain, qualify or resolve. Tell the VO director which job a line performs and where the visual answer lands. Keep the approved continuous script and measured alignment. Use contrast in intent and emphasis rather than perpetual urgency. Do not turn a hypothesis into certainty through a triumphant delivery or sound cue.
46	
47	Natural sound, verified interview audio and motivated effects can connect thoughts when their provenance and actual event timing support that use. A sound bridge can carry the same action over a cut. Sound can't imply recorded access to a site we did not visit. Preserve intelligibility and all existing audio checks.
48	
49	Retain complete captions. Keep extra labels short and attached to the object they identify. Do not present a second paragraph, a busy diagram and a new location at the same time as a dense spoken sentence. Seeing, hearing and reading should reinforce the same unfolding account.
50	
51	## Review the actual report
52	
53	The existing critic and scorers reconstruct the story from the current film before consulting the director's rationale. 1	# Explanatory animation
2	
3	Read the [shared visual-storytelling direction](README.md) first.
4	
5	## What this approach does
6	
7	It makes a hidden process or comparison understandable: two inputs contributing different information, a record moving through a decision, or a physical condition producing a visible measurement. Original diagrams and illustration are often the clearest first choice.
8	
9	Choose this approach when the source establishes the relationship but useful observational footage is missing or can't reveal it. The explanation must preserve the source's uncertainty and distinguish a conceptual example from an actual system output.
10	
11	## Research findings and limits
12	
13	Adobe describes the storyboard as a bridge from script to picture, with panels recording action, dialogue and camera requirements, followed by an animatic to examine the sequence. Its guide includes side-by-side storyboard references for Luca and Up. Those links are study examples; we have not claimed a shot analysis of those films here. [Adobe storyboarding guide](https://www.adobe.com/uk/creativecloud/animation/discover/animation-storyboarding.html).
14	
15	The [shared direction's learning research](README.md) motivates coordinated explanation and reduced distraction. It does not prove that more animation improves understanding. The following construction method is a Dispatch recommendation responding to the actual pavement-film defect.
16	
17	## Build the explanation
18	
19	Write the relationship in plain words before choosing objects. For pavement research: surface imagery and depth information reveal different properties of the same road condition. This is a comparison of information, not a story about two blocks traveling on a conveyor.
20	
21	1. **Show the input.** Give it a recognizable form. A photograph should look like a surface image. A document should have a credible readable structure. A road should look like a road.
22	2. **Introduce one distinction.** Use short labels next to the relevant views. Keep the same sample identity and orientation.
23	3. **Show the operation.** Reveal a cross-section, align corresponding views or trace a source-supported relationship. The operation must change what the viewer can understand.
24	4. **Show the result.** Keep the resulting distinction readable. Do not hide it beneath captions, replace it with a flash or move immediately to another object.
25	5. **Show the decision or limit.** Connect the output to the source-backed choice. Leave unproven implementation visibly unresolved.
26	
27	Use arrows to connect a known relationship, not to pretend that an unavailable algorithm has been observed. A bright scan bar is not analysis proof by itself. Do not invent segmentation accuracy, measured depths, confidence percentages or a vendor interface.
28	
29	Choose 2D, 2.5D or 3D based on the relationship. A flat comparison often explains two images best. A cutaway can reveal depth. A three-dimensional scene earns its cost when spatial interaction is the explanation; a beveled box representing an unfamiliar object often adds interpretation work.
30	
31	## Stage and time the picture
32	
33	Make the principal forms identifiable before their transformation. Maintain consistent labels, positions and shape cues. Use color as support, with readable shape or text distinctions as well. Introduce a new concept only after the current relationship is clear.
34	
35	Plan the reveal around the relevant spoken clause, then use measured narration timing for the final event windows. Quiet or restrained sound can mark a visible comparison; a synthetic beep can't imply actual hardware recording. Preserve the existing sound and caption contracts.
36	
37	A changed state can be information made visible. It need not be a moving human or a mechanical handoff. The current minimum picture-action contract still applies: a full-film static diagram with decorative fades is a rejected treatment.
38	
39	## Worked pattern
40	
41	| Spoken idea | Useful picture | Inadequate substitute |
42	| --- | --- | --- |
43	| A photo shows the surface | A recognizable top-down pavement image | An unlabeled gray slab |
44	| Depth adds another kind of information | Corresponding depth view or disclosed conceptual cutaway | A floating yellow rail |
45	| Damage differs from a stain | Stable side-by-side comparison with the difference revealed | Two different props swapping places |
46	| The result supports a report | A recognizable illustrative report linked to the example | Blank sheets flying into trays |
47	| Detection is not repair | Return to the unchanged physical damage | A celebratory completion animation |
48	
49	This pattern is conceptual guidance, not a verified reconstruction of Texas State's UI or numerical output. See the [pavement case](october-2-pavement-case.md) for source limits.
50	
51	## Before voice and final review
52	
53	Have the existing critic first name the pictured objects and explain the relationship without the director's legend. Then compare exact spoken clauses to rendered moments. If the critic needs the board to identify the principal input or result, consolidate that as a comprehension defect before narration.
54	
55	Use proven components and the existing shared preview comparison. Test the hardest current transformation in the native hero. Preserve the strongest accepted complete treatment as the completion fallback. Additional labels, texture or camera movement can't repair a missing explanation.
56

35	bounded-release route. The [October 2nd pavement diagnosis](visual-storytelling/october-2-pavement-case.md)
36	is a sampled-frame case study, not a replacement verdict or permission to alter the shipped film.
37	
38	## Treatment recovery from September 30, 2026
39	
40	September 29 is a rejected creative reference. Its source screenshots, repeated fading boxes
41	and growing underlines never became an engaging film. Use the source to discover a physical
42	task, obstacle and consequence. Preserve that action in the script and pictures. Authentic
43	imagery earns a shot when it reveals something; a relevant document is not automatically
44	the film's subject. Original source-grounded illustration and demonstrated action remain
45	first-class choices. Reuse proven components, never prior-edition photographic assets.
46	
47	Start with one credible demonstrated treatment and one genuinely different visual treatment.
48	Compare their action, composition and viewer payoff in the existing batch. If both fail,
49	use one consolidated mechanism-changing simplification before narration; do not keep tuning
50	the same weak presentation. Preserve the strongest accepted complete preview as the fallback.
51	No extra research pass, reviewer role, third speculative concept or bespoke rig is authorized.
52	
53	The existing critic must judge the whole film against the prior successful visual standard.
54	Named cities, correct labels and readable source text do not establish strong picture or place.
55	A code pass for geometry and provenance does not establish an engaging treatment. Inspect
56	the opening, middle and ending as actual action before refining layout. Give each cut its own
57	visible reason; repeated prose cannot direct ten different shots.
58	
59	## Choose the story from its tangible stakes
60	
61	Before narration, selected.visual_stakes records affected_person, physical_subject,
62	visible_change, consequence, opening_question, answer, asset_fit and source_urls. Name the
63	specific worker, resident or group and what changes for them. Tie the opening question to the
64	answer that the available evidence can support. A large announcement without useful pictures
65	is a weaker candidate than a smaller action with a visible consequence.
66	
67	Inspect the real site, equipment, people, workflow and records during the existing bounded
68	visual search. Prefer the most informative authentic image. Apply the no-repeat policy in
69	DAILY_PRODUCTION.md. Use source-still or source-excerpt candidate rows with asset_url and the
70	same inspection/rights evidence as source-footage. Diagram rows need a sourced relationship
71	and disclosure Illustration. These are additional media, not permission to invent a workflow.
72	
73	## Choose the medium from the evidence
74	
75	Set cinema.version from the new policy. Keep hero_scene_id, optional hero_passage_end_scene_id,
76	visible_action, human_consequence and source_limit. dimensional_scene_ids is an exact inventory
77	of the quality_plan scenes using 3D; an empty list is legitimate. Each scene still needs a
78	filmable subject, action, consequence and source_basis. Geometry is useful when depth or contact
79	explains something. Footage is useful when the action is actually visible. A still can establish
80	a real place; an excerpt can expose the decisive words; a diagram can explain a sourced relation.
81	Do not force a character into a source image or draw a fake room to meet a quota.
82	
83	The editorial-v1 route accepts each scene's picture with id, medium, event_id, disclosure and
84	subject (the inspected subject, checked by the critic). Use camera_strategy sourcePicture and
85	empty planes for this route's non-dimensional scenes. visual_proof.must_show binds picture.id.
86	Footage/stills/excerpts require file and sha256 from native_media; footprint, provenance and
87	rights remain mandatory. Footage also supplies trim_start_s, trim_end_s, creator, source_url,
88	license_url or its existing editorial_excerpt evidence. It plays at original speed with its
89	original audio muted. Deliberate environmental audio is separately sourced and mixed.
90	
91	A crop is static x/y percentages. A focus box uses x/y/width/height percentages of the displayed
92	frame and reveals on event_id. Use it to reveal a real detail, never imply a machine detected it.
93	Source-excerpt renders the actual inspected page image, preserving its words. Diagram nodes
94	carry short label and claim_id; two to four nodes appear on the event clock. The source and
95	numeral gates cover those printed labels. No long paragraphs or substitute dashboards.
96	Dimensional scenes omit picture and call the existing demonstrated action route; bespoke
97	source-backed mechanisms retain their admission and native-hero requirements.
98	
99	Every current scene receives full-resolution normal/subject-removed sample pairs. The existing
100	proof key without_stage now removes the principal picture for each medium. It never removes
101	captions or branding to manufacture visible action. A source still/excerpt may have a justified
102	intentional_hold within the policy duration after the opening; the phone and final lenses still
103	judge its purpose. Otherwise the principal picture must visibly develop on its event clock.
104	The hero remains a finished native passage with sound, even when it uses no 3D.
105	
106	## Compare two openings once
107	
108	Prepare opening-a.json and opening-b.json beside storyboard.json. From September 30, both may
109	change the complete visual treatment, including the middle and ending. Keep the same dated
110	facts, narration, scene ids and timing, shared inspected asset set and viewer question. Their
111	full visual concepts are hash-bound, including body scenes; retiming does not change identity.
112	For September 29 captures only, the original first-scene-only comparison remains reproducible.
113	Make genuinely different visual approaches. Keep both inside the source and medium contracts.
114	The existing independent code critic reviews both in one reserved assignment and returns
115	opening-a-critic.json and opening-b-critic.json using the ordinary exact concept/renderer/story
116	bindings. It can reject both before a render is spent. Do not add another reviewer identity.
117	
118	Run scripts/opening_compare.py once. It reserves one preflight batch, renders exactly two
119	quarter-scale full animatics with one browser/bundle, and saves openings/comparison.json.
120	Both completed films receive exact-board, film, renderer and inspector-bound structural reports
121	before phone review. The comparison retains both reports and all failures, even if the first
122	inspection fails. Cached comparisons inspect the retained bytes without another render. The
123	normal command exits nonzero on inspection failure. Its --retain-failed-inspection flag retains
124	diagnostics for policy-authorized finishing only; it does not change a failed report or approve
125	phone review. These inexpensive options share the same narrative, so the chosen full preview is
126	already available for continuity review. Failed attempts stay charged. A changed batch requires
127	the existing consolidated repair path, never an automatic reset.
128	
129	For a retained capture from the reviewed pre-inspection orchestration version, use
130	opening_compare.py --inspect-retained. This performs no render or reservation. It verifies the
131	known original orchestration hash, every unchanged capture dependency, both original films and
132	boards, the renderer and source assets, and the original charged reservation. It archives the
133	original comparison and keeps its producer hash, then binds new inspection reports separately.
134	The existing independent selection may keep its original comparison hash only while the exact
135	original capture record is unchanged. Unknown capture versions or changed dependencies refuse
136	adoption. Failed measurements remain failed under this path too.
137	
138	The existing exact-phone critic watches both openings, then the chosen whole sequence. It writes
139	openings/selection.json with comparison_sha256, selected (a or b), director_identity,
140	reviewer_identity, reason, rejected_reason and blocking_defects. Reasons describe observed
141	pixels and the opening question. Copy the chosen frozen board to storyboard.json and its film
142	to preflight.mp4; retain its matching code critique as storyboard_critic.json, inspect that exact
143	film with preflight_animatic --inspect-only, then record the ordinary phone verdict on those
144	bytes. The unused option stays as evidence. Neither option authorizes a narration take until
145	the chosen cut passes the current phone gate. No third concept or extra panel by default.
146	
147	## Direct performance, sound and cuts together
148	
149	creative_direction binds policy_sha256 and records viewer_question, visible_answer,
150	emotional_turn and medium_choice. Its ordered edits rows contain scene_id, enter_on, leave_on,
151	cut_after_event_id and next_connection. The actual event must complete before the cut; a prose
152	promise cannot substitute for its clock. Describe the visible instant that earns each cut and the carried subject
153	or sourced relationship. The final row states the resolved answer and source limit. After any
154	structural change, review the whole sequence. Measured narration retimes the event clock; do not
155	add dead air to preserve an arbitrary grid or accelerate the voice to rescue too many words.
156	
157	creative_direction.sound records perspective, music_arc, voice_arc and cues. Each cue has id,
158	event_id, role (environment, contact, sonification or quiet), duration_s, intent and provenance.
159	Use truthful recorded ambience or an explicitly designed effect. Do not pretend a generated
160	sound was recorded at the actual site. Avoid a hit at every cut. Include one deliberate background
161	contrast with a quiet cue and gain from the policy contract. The quiet cue reduces the music and
162	effects bus on its actual visual event; it never mutes, stretches or splices the narration.
163	
164	Each non-quiet cue has one sfx_events entry with matching id/event_id, wav, source and gain.
165	The mixer anchors it to the current board event, trims to its declared duration at original
166	speed, adds short edge fades and refuses undersized or nonfinite audio. It records every cue,
167	source WAV hash and the exact sound/timing digest in mix.json. Retime the sfx event file with the
168	board and remix after a changed clock. Old mix evidence fails the release check.
169	
170	The existing voice director reads this sound arc and the selected opening. It binds
171	sound_direction_sha256 to the sound object and gives each line specific intent, relative energy
172	and an exact spoken emphasis phrase. Contrast curiosity, discovery and the final consequence
173	without a trailer voice. Numeric pause commands stay out of the TTS prompt. One continuous take
174	and its existing audible soundcheck remain the default; field completion cannot approve a flat
175	or synthetic read. The sound lens judges actual delivery, masking, sync and contrast in the MP4.
176	
177	All three final audiovisual lenses and scoring agents remain. The legacy response field
178	dimensional_action describes the principal picture in any medium. A judge may reject a weak
179	image, inert diagram, generic read or unearned cut with timestamped evidence; a medium preference
180	alone is not a defect. Passing quality moves directly to release and verified shipment.

2	#
3	# Never restate this number in a prompt, a brief, or a verdict file. The sibling lost five panel
4	# rounds to exactly that: its routine prompt carried one number while this file carried another,
5	# so the panel was briefed the stale one and returned ship:false on a cut that was already over
6	# the real bar. Two judges flagged the divergence unprompted and the run kept grading against the
7	# wrong number anyway.
8	#
9	# A number restated in a second place is a number that will be wrong in one of them.
10	#
11	# AND THIS HEADER PROVED IT ON 2026-08-19. It used to tell that story by quoting both numbers,
12	# so the file whose whole job is to hold one bar carried two more in its own comment, four lines
13	# under the sentence forbidding it. The owner moved the bar that morning and all three judges of
14	# round 22 reported being briefed the old one; every one of them also flagged that a judge who
15	# skims this header before reaching the value below reads the stale figure as live. The numerals
16	# are gone. Anyone who needs the number reads the field.
17	#
18	# WHY THE BAR CAME DOWN OFF THE ORIGINAL. The sibling recalibrated with the reason written down:
19	# the original was implicitly calibrated against a painterly fidelity this brand deliberately
20	# does not use, so the ceiling on every run became the house style itself, and the panel's
21	# weakest axis was "the flat vector characters" for nine straight rounds while every concrete
22	# defect got fixed. A bar that can only be cleared by abandoning the house style is not a bar,
23	# it is a disagreement about the style, and it belongs in a style decision rather than a score.
24	rubric:
25	  # Set by the owner on 2026-08-19, down from where it had been.
26	  # This is the ONLY place the bar lives and the only place it may be changed.
27	  # A run does not get to move it: a below-bar final panel remains active repair,
28	  # and delivery requires the hash-bound passing report. Only verified shipment
29	  # completes a production run. The owner controls any change to this bar.

33	    hook:
34	      weight: 0.18
35	      asks: >
36	        Would a stranger stop scrolling in the first two seconds, with the sound off? The first
37	        frame is the whole decision. A title card is not a hook.

39	      weight: 0.20

41	        Does this feel like Texas AI Docket moving today: a dated actor, decision or application,
42	        consequence, honest limit, and what happens next? Is there an earned take rather than a
43	        summary, and does the piece turn somewhere the viewer did not see coming?
44	    picture:
45	      weight: 0.20
46	      asks: >
47	        Does every five seconds pay in motion, emotion or revelation? Is anything a held slide
48	        with a voice over it? With captions hidden, does each shot literally depict the sentence
49	        being spoken rather than reuse generic Texas scenery?
50	    place:
51	      weight: 0.14
52	      asks: >
53	        Would a Texan from that county believe the person who drew this had been there? Region
54	        light, vegetation, kit and cast all correct for the story's actual county.
55	    craft:
56	      weight: 0.14
57	      asks: >
58	        Camera movement motivated by the action; deliberate holds when the subject acts or evidence
59	        is read. Depth and sound clarify cause and consequence. Type legible at feed size. Nothing
60	        symmetric that should not be. Maintained but worn, not new and not ruined.

=== board_diff
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""board_diff.py — what a board edit actually did, in the units the viewer sees.

THE FAULT THIS EXISTS FOR, and it is mine rather than the film's.

A board edit is written in board units: `w 520 -> 240`, `z 1150 -> 3104`, `scale 0.22 -> 1.0`.
What reaches a viewer is screen pixels after projection, and the two are related by arithmetic
nobody was doing at edit time. So on 2026-08-19 a run repeatedly made an edit, described the
edit accurately, watched every gate go green, and shipped something other than what it said:

  - "move the floor behind the racks" DELETED the floor from two interiors, because the code
    emptied the plane before moving it. Eleven gates green.
  - "push the block to z=3104 to hold its framing" made the building VANISH behind the horizon
    band. Legal geometry, correct arithmetic, no object left in the frame.
  - "put the bucket truck at true scale" made it 2065 px wide in a 1080 px frame.
  - "raise groundY to kill the dead sky" hid the building, twice, in the same run.

Every one was caught by eye, three of them only after a fourteen minute render, and one of them
only because a judge reported it two rounds later. None was caught by a gate, because each edit
was individually legal. **The defect was never the value. It was the gap between what the edit
was supposed to do and what it did.**

So this reports the CONSEQUENCE of an edit rather than the edit:

    python3 scripts/board_diff.py --before /tmp/board.before.json --after out/dispatch/storyboard.json

It prints, per item, projected height and screen position before and after, and it flags the
four shapes that have actually bitten: something disappeared, something appeared, something
changed size by more than a third, something left the frame.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""storyboard_check.py — Gate 0. The last cheap place to fix a film.

WHY THIS EXISTS

Everything after this point costs a render. A board that passes here and is wrong
costs an hour; the same fault caught here costs a paragraph. So this runs BEFORE any
scene code exists, and the `storyboard-critic` agent runs after it, on the objective
facts this establishes rather than on vibes.

It checks what can be checked mechanically. Taste is the critic's job and this file
does not pretend to have any.

THE DEFECTS IT IS FOR, each one seen for real.

  A RELABEL PRETENDING TO BE DIVERGENCE. Six scenes that all say dollyThrough over
  the same six planes with the same hero, differing only in the caption. On the page
  it reads as a varied board because the words differ. On screen it is one shot
  played six times. So divergence is measured on the COMPOSITION SIGNATURE, not on
  the label.

  A STATIC CAMERA. The engine's whole value is a composed move through real depth. A
  scene that declares no move wastes it, and a board full of them is a slideshow.

  A FILM THAT PAYS IN ONE CURRENCY. The showstopper standard says every five seconds
  pays in motion, emotion or revelation. A board where every scene says "motion" has
  no turn in it and nobody remembers an image from it.

  A GAP. Scenes that do not tile the runtime leave dead air that nobody notices until
  the mix, when it is expensive.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""place_check.py: a current film stands in its county's region, and its episode lets it show.

WHY THIS EXISTS

PlaceStage (video-engine/src/modern/PlaceStage.tsx) draws each scene's region behind the episode:
outdoors the region's plate fills the frame, indoors it is outside a window in the back wall. That
is only worth anything if a viewer can see it, and every episode is authored new for its story. An
episode that paints a full-frame background of its own, as both episodes on the route did before
October 9th, 2026, hides the region completely, and the film looks exactly as it did when place was
the show's weakest axis. No board field and no code review says so. A render does.

So this renders the film's own frames with the plate replaced by solid magenta (the board's
`__placeProbe`), one still per shot at the point a viewer is most likely to be looking, and counts
the magenta left in the finished frame. A shot that shows less than PLACE_MIN_SHARE of its frame
as region fails, and names the shot. Overhead shots look down at a floor, where no horizon could
show, and source scenes show a source's own picture, so neither is held to it.

It also checks what needs no render: that the plates' manifest holds a plate for every scene's
region, so a story in a region nobody baked fails here rather than throwing in the renderer.

The stage is on for boards dated from the manifest's effective date and for a board that opts in
with its version; for any other board this passes and says the stage is off.

    place_check.py --board out/dispatch/storyboard.json            plates exist for every scene
    place_check.py --board out/dispatch/storyboard.json --render   and the region shows in every shot
    place_check.py --board experiments/modern-film-2026-10-07/board-a.json --opt-in --render

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Re-time the board's cuts to the MEASURED read, so the picture stops running a scene
ahead of the voice.

THE DEFECT THIS EXISTS FOR, and two independent scorers found it in the same round without
seeing each other's notes. The board is authored in Phase 4, before a single word has been
synthesised, and it lays its scenes out on a uniform five second grid because five is a
round number and nothing better is known yet. The read is then synthesised, and it does not
land on that grid, because no human read of eight sentences ever has. Nothing downstream
ever moved the cuts.

The result: for roughly half the runtime the narration described the PREVIOUS shot. The
half built hall, the strongest image in the film, played under the line about the access
notice. The line that names what makes the machine public played over a ranking table. Both
halves were good and they were five seconds apart, which is the most expensive kind of
defect because every gate is green and every asset is correct.

So the cuts move to the words. Each scene declares the `vo` line it was built for, that
line is located in the ALIGNED word stream by matching tokens, and the scene's start is the
measured start of its own first word. Scenes with no line of their own are breathing room
and get interpolated between their spoken neighbours.

WHAT THIS REFUSES, rather than papering over:

- a `vo` line it cannot find in the word stream. A board whose vo text has drifted from the
  script that was actually read is a board whose retime would be a guess, and a confident
  guess here silently re-cuts the film to the wrong places.
- a retime that would make any scene shorter than `--min-scene`. A cut that flashes is
  worse than a cut that is late.
- starts that do not increase. Monotonicity is the one thing a timeline cannot negotiate.

"""engine_lint.py — the defects a TypeScript compiler is structurally blind to.

WHY THIS EXISTS

`tsc` typechecks the engine and says nothing about whether a frame is correct. Every
check below is a real defect that compiled cleanly.

  A CORRUPTED COLOUR LITERAL. `'#2b3category'` and `'#e0b<CJK>88'` both shipped into this
  repo inside otherwise fine-looking palette tables, and both are valid TypeScript
  strings. The browser silently drops an unparseable colour and paints the default,
  so the frame renders and the region is quietly the wrong colour. Two in one session
  is a pattern, and a pattern gets a gate.

  Math.random IN A RENDER. Remotion renders frames independently, so a random value
  draws something different every frame and, worse, differently on a re-render. A
  critic who asks for one fix and gets a different picture back has no way to tell
  whether the fix worked. Every generator in this engine is seeded.

  A STRAIGHT CONDUCTOR. A transmission line between two towers sags in a catenary,
  and a straight line between tower tops is the tell that nobody looked.

  A SYNCHRONISED PUMPJACK FIELD. Every unit in a real field is at a different point
  in its stroke. knowledge/texas/KIT.md leads with it because it is the single most
  recognisable Texas industrial silhouette and the easiest one to get wrong.

  A REGION THAT SHARES A GREEN. The vernacular law is that the Panhandle and Houston
  do not look alike. Two regions with the same vegetation or ground colour is that
  law broken in the one place it is checkable.

    rows += [("script_evidence", ["python", "scripts/script_evidence_check.py", "--board", b, "--claims", c, "--planning-only"]),
             ("super_evidence", ["python", "scripts/super_evidence_check.py", "--board", b, "--claims", c]),
             ("caption_fit", ["node", "video-engine/tests/caption_board_fit.mjs", "--board", b])]
    if modern_film.required(json.loads(Path(board).read_text())):
        rows += [("modern_film", ["python", "scripts/modern_film.py", "--board", b, "--claims", c]),
                 ("native_sample_plan", ["python", "scripts/native_sample_plan.py", "--board", b]),
                 ("story_art", ["python", "scripts/story_art.py", "--board", b, "verify"])]
    return rows


def run_checks(board, claims, out):
    tasks = checks(board, claims)
    directory = Path(out) / str(uuid.uuid4())
    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    rows = []
    for name, args in tasks:
        started = time.monotonic()
        wrapped = ["bash", str(REPO / "scripts/run_with_env.sh"), "bash", "-lc",
                   "cd " + shlex.quote(str(REPO)) + " && exec " + shlex.join(args)]
        result = subprocess.run(wrapped,
                                cwd=REPO, capture_output=True)
        log = directory / (name + ".log")
        log.write_bytes(result.stdout + result.stderr)
        rows.append({"gate": name, "command": args, "exit_code": result.returncode,
                     "elapsed_ms": round((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000),
                     "log": str(log.resolve()), "log_sha256": hashlib.sha256(log.read_bytes()).hexdigest()})
    report = {"schema": "dispatch_picture_precheck/1", "pass": all(row["exit_code"] == 0 for row in rows),
              "checks": rows, "approval": False,
              "note": "Mechanical gate outputs only. Independent code, phone, native, audiovisual and shipment proof remain required."}
    (directory / "report.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n")
    return report, directory


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    p.add_argument("--board", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--claims", type=Path, required=True)
    p.add_argument("--out", type=Path, required=True)
    a = p.parse_args()

44	    """Keep a derived length on its common rounded cut, including half frames."""
45	    if not finite(start) or not finite(end) or start < 0 or end <= start:
46	        raise ValueError('invalid measured shot interval')
47	    start, end = round(start, 4), round(end, 4)
48	    if end <= start:
49	        raise ValueError('measured shot interval vanishes at its declared precision')
50	    duration = end - start
51	    for _ in range(4):
52	        if start + duration == end:
53	            return start, duration
54	        duration = math.nextafter(duration, math.inf if start + duration < end else -math.inf)
55	    raise ValueError('measured shot length cannot reproduce its declared cut')
